Hon'ble Saumitra Dayal Singh,J.
1.

Heard Sri Bhavya Sahai, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and, Sri Anil Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2.
2.

On 18.2.2020, below quoted order was passed:
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 131/2017 arising out of Case Crime No. 0057 of 2016, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 406 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Jhansi pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate/Addl. Civil Judge (J.D.), Court No. 1, Jhansi.

sentences.text: Sri Bhavya Sahai, learned counsel for the applicant states that parties have settled the dispute.
Entire amount has been paid, as agreed between the parties.

Informant herself has made statement at the time of disposal of the bail application no.44842 of 2016 that she does not want to prosecute the applicant and all the cases filed by her against the applicant will be withdrawn after encashment of the bank draft given to her.

It is further contended that proceedings of the aforesaid case be quashed in the light of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh v. State of Punjab :
(2012) 10 SCC 303.
Whether a compromise has taken place or not can best be ascertained by the court where the proceedings are pending, after ensuring the presence of the parties before it.
List this case on 10.4.2020 before the appropriate Bench.
Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes to ensure the presence of both the parties before the court below or any other transferee court, as the case may be, on 25.3.2020 and the court concerned, thereafter, shall ascertain the veracity of the compromise.

entities.text:
Gian Singh v. State of Punjab :
(2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the said compromise is verified, the same shall be made part of the record and report to that effect, will be prepared and the parties would be allowed to obtain certified copy thereof and file the same before this Court.
Office is directed to send through FAX a copy of this order to the court concerned within three days.
Parties are also directed to produce certified copy of this order before the court concerned on the date fixed before it.

Till the next date of listing, no coercive steps would be taken against the applicant."
3.
In compliance thereof, the opposite party no.2 has filed a personal affidavit acknowledging the settlement reached between the parties whereby the matrimonial discord between them has been resolved.
At present, the parties have dissolved their marriage.

The applicant has paid Rs.
20,00,000/- to the opposite party no.2.
In view of such development, opposite party no.2 states, she has no dispute with the present applicant and for that she does not wish to press the prosecution either.

4. In such circumstances, though no useful purpose would be served in allowing the prosecution to continue any further, however, no firm conclusion may be reached, at this stage, as to complete falsity of the allegations made against the applicants.
The present 482 Cr.P.C. application thus stands allowed.

5. Subject to the above, the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 131/2017 arising out of Case Crime No.
0057 of 2016, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 406 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana,
